questions.q: According to the Philippine Green Building Code, what is the minimum required Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) for building metal roof surfaces?
o: A minimum SRI of 65.
A minimum SRI of 75.
A minimum SRI of 80.
A minimum SRI of 70.
questions.n: The Philippine Green Building Code specifically mandates a minimum SRI of 70 for metal roofing to ensure sufficient heat rejection.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of requiring a high SRI for roofing materials?
o: To increase the structural longevity of the metal sheets by preventing thermal expansion.
To minimize heat transfer into the building and reduce cooling loads (energy consumption).
To maximize the capture of solar radiation for integrated rooftop photovoltaic systems.
To prevent oxidation and corrosion caused by UV radiation on the roof surface.
questions.n: Higher SRI means more solar energy is reflected away, reducing the amount of heat entering the building and the electricity needed for air conditioning.

questions.q: Which specific material type is explicitly mentioned in the code as being subject to this SRI 70 requirement?
o: Metal roof surfaces.
Concrete roof slabs.
Clay roof surfaces.
Asphalt shingle surfaces.
questions.n: The requirement specifically targets metal roofing because of its high heat conductivity and common use in the Philippines.

questions.q: What is the typical SRI range for a "Reflective White" roof?
questions.n: Reflective White is the highest tier mentioned, typically providing an SRI range between 86 and 92.

questions.q: Between a "Basic White" and a "Beige/Tan" roof, which is more likely to exceed the minimum requirement of the GB Code?
o: Neither, as both are designed specifically to hit the baseline of 70.
Basic White, because Beige/Tan usually fails the minimum 70 SRI threshold.
Basic White (SRI 80–88), though both technically meet the minimum requirement of 70.
Beige/Tan (SRI 74–80), as it balances absorption and reflection more effectively.
questions.n: Both meet the requirement of 70, but Basic White has higher SRI values (80-88) compared to Beige/Tan (74-80).

questions.q: True or False: A roof with a "Light-to-Medium Green" color is generally compliant with the Philippine Green Building Code’s minimum SRI requirement.
o: False (Typically SRI 30–63).
True.
questions.n: Green, blue, and grey roofs usually have SRI values significantly lower than the required 70.

questions.q: What is the typical SRI range for "Beige/Tan" roofing materials?
questions.n: Beige/Tan materials fall in the 74–80 SRI range, making them compliant with the code.

questions.q: Why are darker roof colors, such as red, generally discouraged under the Green Building Code?
o: Red pigments interfere with the water quality of rainwater collection systems.
They are significantly more expensive to maintain due to pigment fading from UV exposure.
They have lower SRI values, meaning they absorb more heat and increase the "Urban Heat Island" effect.
They cause excessive glare to surrounding mid-rise and high-rise structures.
questions.n: Darker pigments absorb a higher percentage of solar radiation, converting it to heat which affects both the building and the surrounding urban environment.

questions.q: What is the typical SRI range for a "Basic White" metal roof?
questions.n: Basic White typically provides an SRI range of 80 to 88.

questions.q: What is the reported SRI range for Light-to-Medium Green, Blue, or Grey roof colors?
questions.n: These colors are generally non-compliant because their SRI falls between 30 and 63.

questions.q: What index is used to measure a roof's ability to reject solar heat, combined with its ability to emit thermal radiation?
o: Solar Reflectance Index (SRI).
Solar Reflectivity Factor (SRF).
Thermal Emittance Coefficient (TEC).
Heat Reflection Ratio (HRR).
questions.n: SRI is a composite value that accounts for both solar reflectance and thermal emittance.

questions.q: In the context of the GB Code, how does a high SRI value affect the HVAC system of a building?
o: It reduces the cooling load, allowing for lower energy consumption by the air conditioning system.
It requires the installation of high-velocity fans to circulate the reflected cool air.
It increases the humidity levels inside, requiring specialized dehumidification cycles.
It has no effect on HVAC, as SRI is purely an aesthetic building facade requirement.
questions.n: By keeping the building cooler passively, the AC system does not have to work as hard to maintain comfortable temperatures.

questions.q: Which color category provides the highest typical SRI values mentioned (up to 92)?
o: Sky Blue.
Beige/Tan.
Basic White.
Reflective White.
questions.n: Reflective White provides the highest SRI range of 86–92.

questions.q: If a designer chooses a "Grey" roof with an SRI of 55, is this compliant with the Philippine Green Building Code?
o: Yes, if the roof slope is greater than 10 degrees.
No, because grey is considered a dark color regardless of its index.
No (Minimum required is 70).
Yes, provided it is used in a residential zone.
questions.n: The minimum SRI required by the Philippine GB Code is 70; any value below this fails.

questions.q: Does the SRI requirement apply only to the color of the roof, or the performance of the material surface?
o: Only to the visual color spectrum of the paint.
Only to the thickness of the metal roofing material.
The performance of the surface (though color is a major factor in achieving that performance).
To both the surface performance and the chemical composition of the substrate.
questions.n: SRI is a performance metric; while lighter colors help achieve higher values, it is the actual reflection/emittance data that determines compliance.

questions.q: What is the minimum SRI for a roof to be considered "Beige/Tan" according to the provided technical values?
questions.n: The technical range provided for Beige/Tan is 74–80, with 74 being the lower bound.

questions.q: Which color would be the most energy-efficient choice for a warehouse in a tropical climate like the Philippines?
o: Basic White.
Beige/Tan.
Reflective White (SRI 86–92).
Light Blue.
questions.n: Reflective White has the highest SRI value, meaning it rejects the most heat, making it the most energy-efficient.

questions.q: What is the lower limit of the SRI range for a "Reflective White" roof?
questions.n: The range for Reflective White is 86–92, starting at 86.

questions.q: What is the upper limit of the SRI range for a "Light-to-Medium Green/Blue/Grey" roof?
questions.n: The range for these non-compliant colors is 30–63, ending at 63.

questions.q: A "Basic White" roof has a minimum typical SRI of what value?
questions.n: The range for Basic White is 80–88, meaning its typical minimum is 80.

questions.q: Aside from heat transfer to the interior, what environmental phenomenon is mitigated by using high-SRI roofing in cities?
o: Atmospheric acid rain production.
Groundwater contamination through heat-leaching.
The Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect.
The depletion of the local ozone layer.
questions.n: UHI occurs when urban areas become significantly warmer than their rural surroundings; high-SRI roofs reduce the amount of heat the city absorbs.

questions.q: If a metal roof has an SRI of 71, does it pass the Philippine Green Building Code?
o: No, because the code requires a minimum safety factor of 10% above 70.
Yes (It meets the minimum requirement of 70).
questions.n: Since 71 is greater than the required 70, it is technically compliant.

questions.q: Under the code, are "Medium Blue" roofs recommended or discouraged?
o: Recommended, as blue light has shorter wavelengths that dissipate heat faster.
Discouraged (due to low SRI values between 30–63).
questions.n: Blue and other darker colors are discouraged because they fail to meet the SRI 70 requirement.

questions.q: What is the upper SRI limit for "Beige/Tan" roofs?
questions.n: The typical SRI range for Beige/Tan is 74–80, meaning its upper limit is 80.

questions.q: Complete the statement: To comply with the GB Code, a metal roof's SRI must be _____ or higher.
questions.n: The Philippine Green Building Code explicitly sets 70 as the minimum pass value for metal roof SRI.
